newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P 500 futures soar to higher close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P 500 futures soar to higher close.

text.p: U.S. March Standard & Poor's 500s soared to a sharply higher close on active expirations-related buying, traders and analysts said.
"There are a lot of people rolling out their December positions right now," one S&P futures floor source said.

Traders said March's high premium against December encouraged some dealers to roll positions into March. March traded more than seven points above both December and cash S&Ps for most of the session. Fair value was at about 6.50 points.
March S&Ps surged 15.65 points to 753.80 late in the session, above last Thursday's high of 752.50.
Cash S&Ps rose more than 14 points on Thursday for the second largest point gain in history.
Percentage-wise, haowever, the gain did not come close to a record, said Jay Hohmann, head of stock index trading at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
"In terms of percentages, it's actually insignificant," Hohmann said, adding that Thursday's gain represented less than a 2.0 percent increase compared to a 10 percent rise seen one day in 1987.
Traders look for further gains on Friday when the other stock index futures and options, and equity options, expire. The next upward target is at 755.00, last Tuesday's low, traders said.
Hohmann said cash S&Ps traded above a pivotal area around 742.00. The 742.00 level was near the top edge of the market's recent downtrend.
"We broke through that downtrend just a little bit," he said, adding that he'd like to see several more days of gains before determining whether the market broke out from its recent downtrend.
He said a significant level on the upside for cash S&Ps would be at 750.00.

Most floor traders said they expect March S&Ps to continue to rally following the expiration, with several expecting the contract to set the year's highs on the final days of 1996. March's high for the year is at 772.40, which is also the contract and all-time high.
"We've been hitting highs all year," one trader said. "What is different now to change that situation?"
The strength in the U.S. bond market also contributed to the rally in U.S. stocks, traders and analysts said.
However, March Nikkeis ignored the bullish sentiment in U.S. markets and closed sharply lower. March set a contract low earlier in the day at 19,650.

At the end of the day, March S&Ps were up 15.25 at 753.50, New Composites were up 7.70 at 396.15, Value Lines were 9.10 higher at 686.50, Midcap 400s were 3.20 higher at 255.80, Nikkeis were down 310.0 at 19,820 and Nasdaq 100s were 7.50 higher at 857.25.
